# Blackbox

> Open-source ESP32-C3 vehicle telemetry: GPS + WT901 IMU, Rust sensor fusion, browser dashboard, circuit/stage lap timing, and local recordings.

## Project
- [Website and USB installer](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/): project overview and verified published firmware installation.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/jctoledo/blackbox): maintained code, README, issues, and contribution history.
- [Releases](https://github.com/jctoledo/blackbox/releases): published firmware; releases can lag main.

## Documentation
- [Lap timer](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/lap-timer.html): record tracks, arm timing, and troubleshoot missed starts.
- [Sensor fusion](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/sensor-fusion.html): frames, prediction, correction, and limitations.
- [Engineering review](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/engineering-review.html): tested fixes, claims audit, open issues, and hardware acceptance plan.

## Accuracy and status
Blackbox is in active development. Millisecond timestamps and interpolated crossings are not millisecond physical-accuracy claims. The estimator uses diagonal covariance, not a full covariance EKF. Synthetic tests and cross-compilation do not substitute for reference-timed driving or a real USB flash/boot test. Rates depend on configured hardware and measured processing cadence.

This file is a convenient reading index, not a crawler directive or a guarantee of search or AI inclusion.

- [Hardware acceptance checklist](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/hardware-validation.html): bench, USB, sensors, crossings, accuracy, and recording tests.
- [Compatibility and accuracy FAQ](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/guides/faq.html): supported configurations and explicit limits.
- [Interactive dashboard demo](https://jctoledo.github.io/blackbox/demo.html): synthetic telemetry, not a measurement or accuracy demonstration.
